answer: Storage-backed admission assigns disjoint random data to each account and audits unpredictable chunks against its Merkle root. Replicas named orchard, quill and gale must each answer for different data; one lease cannot cover all three. N compliant identities require N storage allocations plus retrieval bandwidth. Missed audits remove eligibility. This needs incompressible data, retrieval deadlines that prevent on-demand regeneration, and expected audit losses exceeding the gains from discarding data.
